notable_absence.finding: The page names "the query engine timeout" without naming the setting, giving its default, or linking to where it is configured - so a reader cannot find out what the timeout is when they do not set one, nor which of the three settings tiers wins. It also does not state the precedence between the request-level timeout and the node-level one, only that either may apply. The corresponding node-level and cluster-level timeout settings are reachable via the Query Admin and Query Settings REST APIs listed on intro.md, but no link is offered from here.

cross_component_finding:
TIMEOUT IS A COLLIDING NAME ACROSS AT LEAST FOUR CONCEPTS IN THE QUERY CORPUS, and this page introduces a fifth framing. The extraction corpus already holds n1ql:txtimeout (transaction timeout) and n1ql:kvtimeout (KV get timeout) as separate ids from the request-parameter reference. This page's `timeout` is the whole-request timeout. server/current/n1ql-rest-query/index.md documents all three side by side in one table, and additionally notes that kvtimeout doubles as the durability timeout for non-transactional DML ("Durability is also supported for non-transactional DML statements. In this case, the kvtimeout parameter is used as the durability timeout"), so one parameter carries two roles. Plus the node-level engine timeout this page alludes to. Five timers, one word. These must not be merged, and reconciliation may want shouldNotBeConfusedWith edges among them - the registry has the predicate and this is a textbook case for it. I have not asserted those edges here because this page names only one of the five.

Also worth noting for the error model: this is the only response in the batch that returns both a results key and an errors key. "results": [] appears alongside the timeout error, and the signature block is present too. So a timeout is modelled as a query that started producing a result set rather than one that failed outright, which is why it gets its own status value and the retry flag. A client that branches on the presence of errors[] alone would mishandle it. The full error-model synthesis is on intro.json.
version_finding:
1. STALE CONFIGURATION FRAMING. The page describes the node-level timer as one "specified when starting the query engine" - a command-line/start-up framing that predates the node-level settings API. In Server 8.0 the Query Service's node-level settings, including timeouts, are configured at runtime via POST /admin/settings (documented in the Query Admin REST API table on intro.md in this same directory), and cluster-wide via POST /settings/querySettings. The prose therefore describes a configuration mechanism the current documentation set no longer presents as primary. This is a behaviour/framing change between versions that the page has not absorbed; recording it as a version finding rather than a behavesDifferentlyUnder relation because the page states only the old framing, so there is no quotable evidence for the new one on this page.

2. No explicit version or edition marker anywhere on the page. Error code 1080 carries no availableSince note, and the retry flag - which is the sort of field that is added in a specific release - carries none either.
